'''Limilngan''', also known as '''Limil''' and '''Manidja''' (also spelt '''Manitja'''), is an extinct [[Aboriginal Australian language]] of the [[Top End]] of Australia.

==Names and ownership==
The language as well as its speakers are known by three names: [[Limilngan]], Limil and Manidja / Manitja, the latter being an [[exonym]].<ref name = AIATSIS/>

Buneidja is regarded as the same language, and the people are sometimes referred to by this name.<ref name = AIATSIS/>

==Traditional lands==
Limilngan was spoken in the [[Darwin, Northern Territory|Darwin]] hinterland, in the [[Mary River (Northern Territory)]] area of [[Kakadu National Park|Kakadu]].<ref name = AIATSIS/>

The Limilngan language uses the three vowel system; /a/, /i/, /u/. The three sounds can result in allophones as [ɑ, æ], [ɪ], and [ʊ].<ref name="Harvey-2001">{{Cite book |url=https://openresearch-repository.anu.edu.au/bitstream/1885/146134/1/PL-516.pdf |title=A grammar of Limilngan: A language of the Mary River Region, Northern Territory, Australia |last=Mark |first=Harvey |publisher=Pacific Linguistics |year=2001 |isbn=978-0-85883-461-3 |series=Pacific Linguistics 516 |location=Canberra |doi=10.15144/pl-516 |hdl=1885/146134 |hdl-access=free}}</ref>
